item.title: Iran/Hormuz Tue Nov 24 (not previously in feed): (1) IRGC Navy (statement via IRNA; CNBC published 12:05 AM EST = 13:05 Taipei Tue) says three 'offending' oil tankers suffered explosions and fires after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz - one near the southern coast, two in the eastern part - despite US military air cover and escort; IRGC: US escort 'will not replace compliance' with its Traffic Control Center instructions. (2) IRGC says a fourth tanker hit a mine after 'unauthorised' passage (Middle East Eye 12:38 GMT = 20:38 Taipei). (3) Iranian Navy (Tasnim, 14:09 Tehran time = 18:39 Taipei) says two more tankers that switched off AIS entered a prohibited zone east of the strait early Tuesday, hit mines, caught fire and were disabled; Navy says the waterway 'would never reopen until Iran's objectives and demands are achieved'. Whether the Navy and IRGC counts overlap = UNKNOWN. (4) Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf (IRNA via Dawn, updated 02:24 pm PKT = 17:24 Taipei): no negotiations with the US until Iran's seven conditions are met (incl. end of hostilities, lifting sanctions and the naval blockade, release of frozen assets). Independent confirmation of the mine strikes, vessel names and casualties = UNKNOWN; US CENTCOM comment = UNKNOWN; oil/gold/FX reaction attributable to these claims = UNKNOWN (gold fell ~2.4% Tue, see snapshot item)

item.title: NY Fed President John Williams (speech 'The Economic Mixdown', Univ. of Mount Saint Vincent, Mon Nov 23; CNBC published 4:00 PM EST = 05:00 Taipei Tue): inflation ~3.5% (Iran conflict/energy, AI build-out demand, tariffs - tariff effects 'largely abated'); 'getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential ... We must take actions over time ... There is still work to do'; forecasts growth ~2-3/4% this year and next, unemployment edging to ~4%, inflation just above 2% in 2027 and 2% in 2028; 'Monetary policy cannot move ships or reopen pipelines...' To reporters after the speech (investingLive): would not rule out hikes at consecutive meetings if needed, no set timing/path, data-driven; tech volatility has not changed his positive outlook, a big darkening in sentiment could. He did not explicitly address December (CNBC). CNBC: likely the last major Fed policy remarks before Dec 8-9 FOMC; current range 3.75%-4.00%. item.title: Fed Governor Cook speech 'The U.S. Economy in Global Context' (Central Bank of Chile annual conference, Santiago; Fed posted 17:15 GMT Fri Nov 20 = 01:15 Taipei Sat Nov 21). On policy: she supported September's hike to 3.75-4.00%, DISSENTED in October preferring another +25bp; 'In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but ... we do not have that luxury'; 'skeptical that September's single 1/4 point rate increase will be enough'; inflation data since September (incl. last week's reports) 'fail to provide me with sufficient evidence' inflation is returning to a sustainable path; 'waiting longer ... risks getting behind the curve. If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later'; number and magnitude of future adjustments to be informed by the economy's reaction. Outlook: growth 'strong - and accelerating' (Q3 GDP 3.4% annualized), est. Oct PCE 3.8% y/y / core 3.2%, inflation above 2% for 67 months, unemployment 4.1%, Oct payrolls +165k, claims 4-wk avg ~195k; financial conditions 'too accommodative', AI buildout not curtailed. She did NOT state a specific December move or size (Yahoo Finance: 'stopped short'); Reuters: markets broadly expect a December 8-9 hike. Interpretation (not her words): hawkish, consistent with at least +25bp in December; explicit 50bp call = UNKNOWN/none
